recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further core source work is needed for FHIR-36859 unless the work group wants a separate editorial cleanup unrelated to the resolved semantic clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-36859 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked what a conditional update should do when the search finds no matching resources, the incoming resource has an id, and a resource with that same id already exists on the server. The resolution split the no-match/id-provided case into an Update as Create path when that id does not already exist and a 409 Conflict rejection when that id already exists.
initial_application: Git commit e76c0dd6aa055fe1ad4d07c56cee8784707220b0 explicitly applied FHIR-36859 to source/http.html by splitting the no-match/id-provided bullet into the two approved cases. Later commits 9db1c10f97bbd396ea035531fec1e53dc12b22cd and ee761ef4bd5a52057846f25556c859510db5375c normalized HTTP status-code markup while preserving the same behavior.
additional_context: Earlier Published issues FHIR-17906 and FHIR-20390 are the same conditional-update decision-table family: FHIR-17906 split the original no-match behavior into no-id and id-provided cases, and FHIR-20390 clarified that id provided means Resource.id. FHIR-I WGM 202205 minutes record the FHIR-36859 Persuasive with Modification vote. Targeted Zulip searches found no later or conflicting community discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/http.html already says that when no search matches are found and the provided id does not already exist, the server treats the request as Update as Create or rejects it if unsupported, and when no search matches are found and the provided id already exists, the server rejects the update with 409 Conflict. A minor grammatical difference from the Jira resolution does not alter implementer understanding.
